summary: Provides a PICS proforma for version 3 of the Network Time Protocol, a conformance checklist implementers fill in to state which features they support. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A form where makers of clock-syncing software tick boxes to show which features they have.

questions: how do ntp implementations declare conformance
what is a protocol conformance statement
subtitle: A checklist form for NTP implementations to declare supported features

tldr.problem: When evaluating whether an NTP implementation is compliant with the NTP version 3 specification, there is no standard way to document which features and options a particular implementation supports.
tldr.mechanism: A PICS proforma is a structured form that NTP implementers fill in to declare which features they support, using mandatory (m), optional (o), and conditional (c) entries organized by topic.
tldr.outcome: Developers, users, and testing organizations can easily understand the capabilities of different NTP implementations and make informed decisions about deployment. The proforma became a reference for conformance evaluation of NTP v3 systems.

today: RFC 1708 is Informational and has not been obsoleted. It remains the standard PICS proforma for NTP version 3, though NTP has evolved with newer versions published in subsequent RFCs.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Protocol Implementation Conformance Statements (PICS) are standardized forms used to document the capabilities of protocol implementations. RFC 1708 provides the PICS proforma for Network Time Protocol version 3, the protocol that synchronizes computer clocks across networks. The proforma is based on ISO/IEC 9646 conformance testing methodology, ensuring consistency with international testing standards.

The document serves as a template that developers and implementers can use to formally declare what features they have implemented in their NTP systems. This allows users, network operators, and testing organizations to compare different NTP implementations and understand their capabilities without needing to read source code.
sections.eli5: PICS is like a reference sheet where software makers write down what their program can do, so people know what features to expect.

sections.title: The PICS Proforma Structure
sections.content:
The proforma is organized into major sections covering different aspects of NTP v3 implementation. It begins with fields for implementation identification, including the supplier name, contact information, implementation name and version, and system details. This allows clear identification of which product or system is being described.

The core of the proforma consists of tables that organize NTP requirements into categories: data formats, state variables and parameters, filtering and selection algorithms, local clock implementations, NTP data format fields, and NTP control messages. Each requirement is listed with a status indicator showing whether it is mandatory (m), optional (o), or conditional (c) for compliance.

The conditional requirements include notes explaining when they apply (for example, certain features are mandatory if authentication is used, while others are only mandatory for implementations intended for use on the Internet). This structure allows for flexibility while ensuring that all necessary combinations are documented.
sections.eli5: The form divides NTP into sections for time stamps, variables, algorithms, clock types, message formats, and control messages, with each feature marked as required, optional, or conditional.

sections.title: Data Formats and State Variables
sections.content:
NTP uses several key pieces of information to synchronize time. The proforma lists all the required data elements, starting with the 64-bit timestamp format that carries time information. It then documents state variables at multiple levels: common variables like peer addresses and stratum, system-wide variables such as the local clock, peer-specific variables for tracking synchronization with particular time sources, and packet variables that are set in each NTP message.

The proforma includes comprehensive tables for clock filter variables used to select the best time source from multiple peers, and authentication variables for cryptographic authentication of NTP messages. Each variable is marked with its reference to the NTP v3 specification so implementers can verify they understand the requirement correctly.

Parameter values are also listed, including standard values like NTP port 123, maximum stratum of 15, and polling interval ranges. These concrete values help ensure consistent behavior across different implementations.
sections.eli5: The form lists all the time stamps, network addresses, clock information, and security settings that an NTP system needs to track.

sections.title: Modes, Procedures and Algorithms
sections.content:
NTP v3 supports multiple modes of operation: symmetric active and passive modes for peer relationships, client mode for requesting time from a server, server mode for providing time, and broadcast mode for one-way dissemination. At least one mode must be implemented, but implementations can support any combination. The proforma explicitly marks this requirement as optional with a note that at least one is mandatory.

The proforma documents event processing procedures: transmit and receive procedures for handling NTP messages, packet processing, clock update operations, and initialization. It also covers optional procedures like authentication during these operations, and optional features like control messages used for network management and monitoring of NTP systems.

Additional sections cover clock filtering procedures that select the best time source among multiple peers, clock selection algorithms that combine multiple time sources, and local clock implementations with specific parameters for different hardware approaches (crystal oscillator-based or system-clock based). Phase adjustment procedures for gradual and step changes to the system clock are also documented.
sections.eli5: The form shows which time synchronization modes (client, server, broadcast) are supported, what procedures are used for sending and receiving messages, and how the system picks the best time source.

sections.title: Conformance Testing and Use
sections.content:
The proforma is designed for conformance evaluation of NTP v3 implementations. Suppliers fill it in to formally declare their implementation's capabilities, and the completed forms become part of the documentation for that product. This allows comparison between products and helps ensure that systems claiming to implement NTP v3 actually do so consistently.

The document includes a copyright notice explicitly allowing anyone to reproduce and distribute the proforma, and to freely publish completed PICS forms. This ensures the proforma can be widely used without licensing restrictions. The use of ISO standards methodology provides a common language that works across different organizations and countries for evaluating conformance.

RFC 1305, which defines NTP v3 itself, provides all the normative details, and RFC 1708 references it throughout. Implementers are expected to have the NTP v3 specification available and to carefully review each requirement before filling in the proforma. When a requirement is marked as conditional, the notes clarify exactly when it applies.
sections.eli5: Implementers fill out the form to officially say what their NTP version 3 system can do, and it helps people check if software meets the standard.

references.text: Mills, D., "Network Time Protocol Version 3 - Specification, Implementation and Analysis", RFC 1305, UDEL, March 1992.
